headline: High-risk default filesystem and web-search coupling: Open Interpreter can expose local files to Perplexity-driven workflows, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads the local filesystem and clipboard by default, while Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context. If content from Open Interpreter is copied or saved into Perplexity, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. The pair has a documented pairing, but no provenance isolation is shown.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter output is copied into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity treats uploaded text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of agent output into prompts
Use a separate scratch file for untrusted text
Add a manual review step before Perplexity queries
Tag imported content as data, not instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress; Perplexity sends queries and uploaded documents to vendor APIs. In the default pair, local files reachable by Open Interpreter can be forwarded into Perplexity workflows, creating a realistic exfiltration path for secrets or sensitive documents.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter accesses sensitive local files
IF those file contents are pasted or uploaded into Perplexity
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a non-sensitive directory
Avoid uploading local documents to Perplexity
Review prompts for secrets before sending
Use redaction on copied excerpts
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Perplexity can run browsers and maintain shared Space context across sessions. The profiles do not show direct shared write access, but the pair can still contend over shared artifacts if both touch the same workspace or browser-derived outputs.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory
IF browser-derived artifacts are saved back into the shared workspace
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use read-only exports from Perplexity
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from browsing context, and Open Interpreter can act on or transform those outputs with shell and filesystem access. If Open Interpreter treats Perplexity text as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated answer can cascade into irreversible local actions such as edits, installs, or git changes.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter uses Perplexity output as the basis for commands or edits
IF the output is not independently verified before execution
mitigations: Require human verification before execution
Cross-check key facts against a second source
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Keep Perplexity outputs in read-only notes
requires-engineering: add structured verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter can touch anything reachable on the local machine, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is present locally, moving it into Perplexity can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR terms, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF that data is uploaded or pasted into Perplexity
mitigations: Do not upload regulated documents
Strip identifiers before querying
Check vendor retention settings before use
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive data
requires-engineering: formalize a data-handling policy
